title: Minimax Regret for Score-Threshold Policies under Margin and Vanishing Propensities

proof_attempt_summary: The F3 loop built an axiom-clean RowLaw IPW weighted-arm lemma and second-moment bound, repaired the four-chain observation-domain statement, and closed regularization_inequality. The full research barrel builds, but ten source sorry sites remain, including the four-chain moment and measurability lemmas, the upper theorem, and lower-pair and all-procedure arguments. tldr: Known logging does not stabilize score-threshold learning when propensities approach zero. For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(\theta>0\), every Borel score marginal on \([0,1]\), wedge \(v\le u^\gamma\), and tail factor \(v^\theta\), the exact sorted whole-observation-deleted inverse-score selector attains the matched expected welfare-regret power \(r=\min\{(\alpha+1)/(\alpha+2+\alpha\gamma/(\alpha+\theta\gamma)),\theta/(\theta+1)\}\). The learner groups tied scores and needs no supplied or known score distribution function or probability transform. The minimax infimum covers every randomized Borel binary rule that is jointly measurable in data, an independent uniform randomizer, and score for each fixed supplied logger. Same-logger near-tie and retuned high-effect blocks with a uniform marginal prove the all-procedure converse. On \(\theta=1/\gamma\), only the local branch equals the accepted \texttt{stat\_policy\_regret\_margin\_overlap} bank's lower-bound exponent; the whole matched slice and its high-effect branch are present-paper results, not a transferred bank theorem. The sharp regret-quantile frontier remains a separate open problem.
gap: Published policy-learning results use a propensity floor, optimal-policy coverage, fixed-law limits, or online entropy conditions. The nearest banked result fixes \(\alpha=\gamma=1\), one threshold orientation, and excludes zero-effect mass; it does not cover the faster and slower power regimes indexed by general \((\alpha,\gamma)\).
fill: The project derives the two-mechanism phase boundary, constructs an exact observable threshold selector, proves its uniform expected-regret upper bound, and matches it with legal lower pairs sharing the supplied logging function.
